info.title: SadCaptcha TikTok/Shopee/Shein/Temu Captcha Solvers
info.description:
# Overview
This API uses image processing to provide solutions to TikTok, Temu, Shein, Shopee, and more captcha's. 
It is able to solve every TikTok captcha including puzzle, rotate, 3d shapes, and icon (video upload). 
Shopee captcha solvers are available, for the puzzle slide, image crawl, and image drag puzzles. 
We also support captchas for betting sites such as Paripulse, where the user must score a goal by dragging a soccer ball.
## Python client
If you are running Python with Selenium or Playwright, you can skip learning the API and just use our Python client.
### TikTok Python Client
To install the TikTok client, run `pip install tiktok-captcha-solver`.

For instructions on how to use the Python client, see [the official TikTok client repository](https://github.com/gbiz123/tiktok-captcha-solver).
### Shopee Python Client
To install the Shopee client, run `pip install shopee-captcha-solver`.

For instructions on how to use the Python client, see [the official Shopee client repository](https://github.com/gbiz123/shopee-captcha-solver).
### Shein Python Client
To install the Shein client, run `pip install shein-captcha-solver`.

For instructions on how to use the Python client, see [the official Shein client repository](https://github.com/gbiz123/shein-captcha-solver).
## Chrome extension
If you're not a programmer, or need a no-code solution, please install and use our Chrome extension.

The Chrome extension also makes a good option for Puppeteer and Browser Automation Studio (BAS) users.
### TikTok Chrome Extension
The TikTok captcha solver Chrome extension can be installed by loading the source code as an unpacked extension after cloning the [Github repository.](https://github.com/gbiz123/sadcaptcha-chrome-extensino/tree/master)
### Shopee Chrome Extension
The Shopee captcha solver Chrome extension can be installed by loading the source code as an unpacked extension after cloning the [Github repository.](https://github.com/gbiz123/shopee-captcha-solver-chrome-extension)
### Shein Chrome Extension
The Shein captcha solver Chrome extension can be installed by loading the source code as an unpacked extension after cloning the [Github repository.](https://github.com/gbiz123/shein-captcha-solver-chrome-extension)
##  Responses 
This API is designed to work on any device, regardless of device type or screen resolution. While other captcha solving API's return pixel coordinates, SadCaptcha returns proportions and ratios which can be scaled to any resolution.
This offers flexibility and reliability, but there are some conversions that you must do, which will be described in this documentation.
Each response is documented in its respective section of the documentation.
For a working implementation of the API with all captchas implemented, we recommend you look at the code in the Python client repositories listed above.
 ## Sending the images
The images must be sent to SadCaptcha as base64 encoded strings. To do this, you may download the image from the html element's `src` attribute using any HTTP library such as Python `requests`, and then apply the base64 encoding. Python offers a very simple package called `base64` which can handle the encoding in a single line.

## Two image 
![two image](https://sadcaptcha.b-cdn.net/temu-two-image.webp)
### Description 
This challenge appears on Temu and presents two side-by-side images, and a text challenge that explains where you must click. Currently only English is supported.
### Making the API call
```py
import requests
import base64

BASE_URL = 'https://www.sadcaptcha.com/api/v1'
LICENSE_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'


# Build the two image URL
two_image_url = f'{BASE_URL}/temu-two-image?licenseKey={LICENSE_KEY}'

# Prepare the request
data = {
    'challenge': 'Please click on the corresponding chatacters in figure 1 in the order they appear from left to right in figure 2.',
    'imagesB64': ['left image b64 encoded', 'right image b64 encoded']
}

# Get the answer as point ratios
r = requests.post(two_image_url, json=data)

print(r.json())
```
### Using the solution
The solution to the Semantic shapes captcha is returned as a single point, representing where one must click on the image to solve the captcha. The points are represented as **ratios** of the solution coordinate to the total width and length of the image. In other words, the coordinates are normalized to the length of the image.The coordinate (0.0, 0.0) represents the top left corner of the image, and the coordinate (1.0, 1.0) represents the bottom right. The coordinate (0.5, 0.5) represents the center of the image, and so on. The formulas below demonstrate how to convert the point of ratios to a point in pixel space to solve the captcha:

To solve for `x`:
- `x = p_x * w`

Where
- `w` = the width of the captcha image (the element with css selector `.captcha-verify-image`)
- `p_x` = the proportion of x returned by the SadCaptcha API

And to solve for `y`:
- `y = p_y * w`

Where

- `w` = the width of the captcha image
- `p_y` = the proportion of y returned by the SadCaptcha API

## Temu 3x3 (similar to reCaptcha)
### Description
This captcha is seen when using Temu. The challenge is similar to the Recaptcha v2 challenge, where there are 3 rows of 3 images, and you have to select the correct ones. Temu asks you to select certain objects of interest in a particular order. To solve it, you need to send information about the objects of interest and each of the 9 image panels. 
### The request 
The request contains strings representing the objects you must click, and the images as base64 strings. Assuming the challenge is "Click on the corresponding images in the following order: 'television','strawberry','peach'", then the request would look like: 
```
{
"objects_of_interest": [
"television",
"strawberry",
"peach"
],
"images": [
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0K...."
]
}
```
As you can see, the JSON that you send has two lists: the names of the objects of interest, and each image encoded as a base64 string.
### Using the solution
The solution is given as the list of indices of the images you must click.
For example, if the solution is [0, 1, 2] then you must click the first, second, and third images in that order.

## Swap two 
### Description 
This challenge appears on temu. You must swap the two tiles that are out of place. 
### Making the API call
```py
import requests
import base64

BASE_URL = 'https://www.sadcaptcha.com/api/v1'
LICENSE_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'


# Build the icon URL
shapes_url = f'{BASE_URL}/temu-swap-two?licenseKey={LICENSE_KEY}'

# Convert the images to base64 encoding
with open('images/swap.png', 'rb') as f:
    swap_two_url = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

# Prepare the request
data = {
    'imageB64': swap
}

# Get the answer as point ratios
r = requests.post(swap_two_url, json=data)

print(r.json())
```
### Using the solution
The solution to the Swap Two captcha is returned as two points.
 The first point represents where one must press the mouse, and the secon point represents where one must release the mouse after dragging.The points are represented as **ratios** of the solution coordinate to the total width and length of the image. In other words, the coordinates are normalized to the length of the image.The coordinate (0.0, 0.0) represents the top left corner of the image, and the coordinate (1.0, 1.0) represents the bottom right. The coordinate (0.5, 0.5) represents the center of the image. To calculate the pixel location within the image you must click and release, you multiply the values in the response by the width and height of the image element. 
The formulas below demonstrate how to convert the point of ratios to a point in pixel space to solve the captcha:

To solve for `x`:
- `x = p_x * w`

Where
- `w` = the width of the captcha image
- `p_x` = the proportion of x returned by the SadCaptcha API

And to solve for `y`:
- `y = p_y * w`

Where

- `w` = the width of the captcha image
- `p_y` = the proportion of y returned by the SadCaptcha API

## Temu Arced Slide
![arced slide image](https://sadcaptcha.b-cdn.net/temu-arced-slide.webp)
### Description
This captcha is seen when web scraping or automating Temu. The challenge is similar to the puzzle slide challenge, but the slider piece moves in an arc at an unpredictable trajectory. Moreover, there are two possible locations where the slide piece could fit, but only one of them is correcr. Because of this, the API needs to accept both the puzzle and piece images, but also data about the trajectory. The Python client (`pip install temu-captcha-solver`) will automatically determine the slide trajectory and send the necessary data. For non-python applications it is recommended to re-implement the code contained in the `temu-captcha-solver` GitHub repository in your preferred language.
### Getting the slide piece trajectory 
To get the slide piece trajectory, you must slide the slide button over the entire bar, and record the following after each pixel: 
- slide button number of pixels from origin
- slide piece x, y location
- slide piece rotation angle

The location of the slide button is expressed as a proportion where the x location of the button is divided by the total width of the slide bar.
The slide piece x, y location refers to the x, y point at the center of the slide piece's bounding box, where x and y are expressed in terms of the proportion to the width and height of the puzzle image, respectively.
The slide piece rotation angle is the `rotate()` value extracted from the `style` attribute of its HTML element.
If this all sounds very complicated, please look into our Python client or Chrome extension for an already working implementation.
Here is an example of the POST body containing the Base64 images and the slide piece trajectory:
```{"puzzle_image_b64": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgA..."
"piece_image_b64": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAA..."
"slide_piece_trajectory": [
{
"pixels_from_slider_origin": 0,
"piece_rotation_angle": 0.0,
"piece_center": {
"proportion_x": 0.08695652173913043,
"proportion_y": 0.6826086956521739
}
},
{
"pixels_from_slider_origin": 1,
"piece_rotation_angle": -0.841872,
"piece_center": {
"proportion_x": 0.08695652173913043,
"proportion_y": 0.5478260869565217
}
},
{
"pixels_from_slider_origin": 0.01932367149758454,
"piece_rotation_angle": -0.841872,
"piece_center": {
"proportion_x": 0.08695652173913043,
"proportion_y": 0.5478260869565217
And so on for each pixel traveled...
```
### Sending the request 
```pyimport requests
import base64

BASE_URL = 'https://www.sadcaptcha.com/api/v1'
LICENSE_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'


# Build the puzzle URL
puzzle_url = f'{BASE_URL}/temu-arced-slide?licenseKey={LICENSE_KEY}'

# Convert the images to base64 encoding
with open('images/puzzle.png', 'rb') as f:
    puzzle = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()
with open('images/piece.png', 'rb') as f:
    piece = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

# Find the slide piece trajectory
# For the full implementation of finding the slide trajectory, please see the code in the github repo: https://www.github.com/gbiz123/temu-captcha-solver
trajectory = [...]  # Prepare the request
data = {
    'puzzleImageB64': puzzle,
    'pieceImageB64': piece
    'slidePieceTrajectory': trajectory
}

# Get the answer as the solution the ratio of solution distance to total distance of the puzzle
r = requests.post(puzzle_url, json=data)

print(r.json())
```
### Using the solution
The solution is the number of pixels you must travel from the origin of the slider button to the solution.
To use it, drag the slider to that point. Please note that the request must be sent and consumed before you let the slide button up.

## Shopee Image Crawl Pre-Analyze
### Description
This endpoint is a companion to the Shopee Image Crawl solver. Before recording the slide piece trajectory and solving the captcha, you can pre-analyze the puzzle image to determine two useful pieces of information: the version of the challenge (`v1` or `v2`), and the maximum proportion of the slide bar that the piece needs to be dragged. Knowing the maximum drag distance ahead of time allows the client to make more precise movements without dragging the piece all the way to the end of the bar every single time. The Python client (`pip install shopee-captcha-solver`) will automatically call this endpoint and use the result. For non-python applications it is recommended to re-implement the code contained in the `shopee-captcha-solver` GitHub repository in your preferred language.
### Making the API call
```py
import requests
import base64

BASE_URL = 'https://www.sadcaptcha.com/api/v1'
LICENSE_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'


# Build the pre-analyze URL
pre_analyze_url = f'{BASE_URL}/shopee-image-crawl-pre-analyze?licenseKey={LICENSE_KEY}'

# Convert the image to base64 encoding
with open('images/puzzle.png', 'rb') as f:
    puzzle = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

# Prepare the request
data = {
    'imageB64': puzzle
}

# Get the challenge version and the max slide proportion
r = requests.post(pre_analyze_url, json=data)

print(r.json())
```
### Using the solution
The response contains two fields:
- `version` - the version of the image crawl challenge, either `v1` or `v2`.
- `slideXProportion` - the maximum proportion of the slide bar width that the piece needs to be dragged.

Multiply `slideXProportion` by the width of the slide bar to obtain the maximum pixel distance the piece must travel. Use this to bound the trajectory you record before calling the `/shopee-image-crawl` endpoint.

## Shein 3x3 (similar to reCaptcha)
### Description
This captcha is seen when web scraping or automating Shein. The challenge is similar to the Recaptcha v2 challenge, where there are 3 rows of 3 images, and you have to select the correct ones. Shein asks you to select all of the images matching a word or phrase, such as "bananas". To solve it, you need to send the challenge text along with each of the 9 image panels. 
### The request 
The request contains the challenge text, and the images as base64 strings. Assuming the challenge is "Select all images containing bananas", then the request would look like: 
```
{
"challenge_text": "bananas",
"images": [
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0KGgo...",
"iVBORw0K...."
]
}
```
As you can see, the JSON that you send has the challenge text, and a list with each image encoded as a base64 string.
### Using the solution
The solution is given as the list of indices of the images, ranked from the most to the least likely to match the challenge text.
For example, if the solution is [2, 5, 6, 0, 1, 3, 4, 7, 8] then the third image is the best match, followed by the sixth and the seventh. 
Click the images from the start of the list, taking as many of them as the challenge asks you to select.

## Shein Icon 
Shein presents this captcha that requires you to click the icons in the main image in the order they appear in the bar. Here's an example:


![items image](https://sadcaptcha.b-cdn.net/shein-icon-captcha-1.png)
### Getting the captcha image from Shein
The CAPTCHA image is presented as a div with a CSS background-image. 
The image URL can be extracted from the div using: `window.getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.pic_wrapper')).backgroundImage.match(/(?<=").*(?=")/)[0]`.
Once the image URL has been extracted, you can download it using an HTTP request and convert it to base64 to be sent to our API.
### Making the API call
```py
import requests
import base64

BASE_URL = 'https://www.sadcaptcha.com/api/v1'
LICENSE_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'


# Build the icon URL
shapes_url = f'{BASE_URL}/semantic-shapes?licenseKey={LICENSE_KEY}'

# Convert the images to base64 encoding
with open('images/shapes.png', 'rb') as f:
    image = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

# Prepare the request
data = {
    'imageB64': image
}

# Get the answer as point ratios
r = requests.post(shapes_url, json=data)

print(r.json())
```
### Using the solution
The solution to the shein icon captcha is returned as a list of points, representing where one must click on the image to solve the captcha. The points are returned in the order they must be clicked in the image. The points are represented as **ratios** of the solution coordinate to the total width and length of the image. In other words, the coordinates are normalized to the length of the image.The coordinate (0.0, 0.0) represents the top left corner of the image, and the coordinate (1.0, 1.0) represents the bottom right. The coordinate (0.5, 0.5) represents the center of the image, and so on. The formulas below demonstrate how to convert the point of ratios to a point in pixel space to solve the captcha:

To solve for `x`:
- `x = p_x * w`

Where
- `w` = the width of the captcha image
- `p_x` = the proportion of x returned by the SadCaptcha API

And to solve for `y`:
- `y = p_y * w`

Where

- `w` = the width of the captcha image
- `p_y` = the proportion of y returned by the SadCaptcha API

```py
BASE_URL = 'https://www.sadcaptcha.com/api/v1'
LICENSE_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'


# Build the icon URL
shapes_url = f'{BASE_URL}/semantic-items?licenseKey={LICENSE_KEY}'

# Convert the images to base64 encoding
with open('images/shapes.png', 'rb') as f:
    shapes = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

# Prepare the request
data = {
    'challenge': 'Please click the type of electronic device that appears most frequently.',    'imageB64': shapes
}

# Get the answer as point ratios
r = requests.post(shapes_url, json=data)

print(r.json())
```
### Using the solution
The solution to the Semantic items captcha is returned as a single point, representing where one must click on the image to solve the captcha. The points are represented as **ratios** of the solution coordinate to the total width and length of the image. In other words, the coordinates are normalized to the length of the image.The coordinate (0.0, 0.0) represents the top left corner of the image, and the coordinate (1.0, 1.0) represents the bottom right. The coordinate (0.5, 0.5) represents the center of the image, and so on. The formulas below demonstrate how to convert the point of ratios to a point in pixel space to solve the captcha:

To solve for `x`:
- `x = p_x * w`

Where
- `w` = the width of the captcha image 
- `p_x` = the proportion of x returned by the SadCaptcha API

And to solve for `y`:
- `y = p_y * w`

Where

- `w` = the width of the captcha image
- `p_y` = the proportion of y returned by the SadCaptcha API

## Rotate
![rotate image](https://sadcaptcha.b-cdn.net/tiktokrotate.webp)
### Making the API call
```py
import requests
import base64

BASE_URL = 'https://www.sadcaptcha.com/api/v1'
LICENSE_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'


# Build the rotate URL
rotate_url = f'{BASE_URL}/rotate?licenseKey={LICENSE_KEY}'

# Convert the images to base64 encoding
with open('images/outer_tt.png', 'rb') as f:
    outer = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()
with open('images/inner_tt.png', 'rb') as f:
    inner = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

# Prepare the request
data = {
    'outerImageB64': outer,
    'innerImageB64': inner
}

# Get the answer as the solution angle
r = requests.post(rotate_url, json=data)

print(r.json())
```
### Using the solution
The solution to the rotate captcha is given as the **angle** from 0 to 360 that the image must rotate to solve the captcha. The formula to convert the angle to the pixel slide distance is as follows:
- `d = ((l_s - l_i) * a) / 360`

Where
- `l_s` = the total length of the slidebar (the element with css selector `.captcha_verify_slide--slidebar`)
- `l_i` = the length of the slide icon (the element with css selector `.secsdk-captcha-drag-icon`)
- `a` = the solution angle returned by SadCaptcha.

## Puzzle
![puzzle image](https://sadcaptcha.b-cdn.net/tiktokpuzzle.webp)
### Making the API call
```py
import requests
import base64

BASE_URL = 'https://www.sadcaptcha.com/api/v1'
LICENSE_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'


# Build the puzzle URL
puzzle_url = f'{BASE_URL}/puzzle?licenseKey={LICENSE_KEY}'

# Convert the images to base64 encoding
with open('images/puzzle.png', 'rb') as f:
    puzzle = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()
with open('images/piece.png', 'rb') as f:
    piece = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

# Prepare the request

    'puzzleImageB64': puzzle,
    'pieceImageB64': piece
}

# Get the answer as the solution the ratio of solution distance to total distance of the puzzle
r = requests.post(puzzle_url, json=data)

print(r.json())
```
### Using the solution
The solution to the puzzle captcha is given as the **ratio** of the solution slide distance to the total distance of the slide. Use this simple conversion to compute the solution distance:

- `d = r * w`

Where
- `w` = The width of the puzzle image (the element with css selector `.captcha-verify-image`)
- `r` = The ratio value returned by the SadCaptcha API

## Paripulse Soccer
### Description
This captcha is seen when web scraping or automating Paripulse. You are presented with a soccer player and a goal, and you must slide the button left or right until the ball lines up with the goal. The player and the goal move as you drag the slide button, so a single image is not enough to determine the answer. Because of this, the API accepts one screenshot of the captcha for each location of the slide button, and returns the number of pixels from the slider origin that scores the goal.
### Getting the images per location 
To get the images per location, you must slide the slide button over the entire bar, and record the following after each pixel: 
- a base64 encoded screenshot of the captcha image
- the number of pixels the mouse is from the center of the slide bar

The number of pixels from center is negative when the mouse is to the left of the center of the slide bar, and positive when it is to the right.
Here is an example of the POST body containing the base64 images and their locations:
```
{
"imagesPerLocation": [
{
"imageB64": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgA...",
"mousePixelsFromCenter": -120
},
{
"imageB64": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAA...",
"mousePixelsFromCenter": -119
},
And so on for each pixel traveled...
]
}
```
### Sending the request 
```py
import requests
import base64

BASE_URL = 'https://www.sadcaptcha.com/api/v1'
LICENSE_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'


# Build the paripulse soccer URL
soccer_url = f'{BASE_URL}/paripulse-soccer?licenseKey={LICENSE_KEY}'

# Drag the slide button across the bar, taking a screenshot at each pixel
images_per_location = [
    {'imageB64': base64.b64encode(screenshot).decode(), 'mousePixelsFromCenter': pixels_from_center}
    # ...one entry for each pixel traveled
]

# Prepare the request
data = {
    'imagesPerLocation': images_per_location
}

# Get the answer as the number of pixels from the slider origin
r = requests.post(soccer_url, json=data)

print(r.json())
```
### Using the solution
The solution is the number of pixels you must travel from the origin of the slider button to the solution.
To use it, drag the slider to that point. Please note that the request must be sent and consumed before you let the slide button up.

## Paripulse Soccer Pre-Analyze
### Description
This endpoint is a companion to the Paripulse Soccer solver. Before recording one screenshot per slide button location and solving the captcha, you can pre-analyze a single screenshot of the captcha to determine three useful pieces of information: the direction the ball needs to be dragged in (`left` or `right`), the location of the ball, and the location of the goal. Knowing the direction ahead of time allows the client to drag the slide button only towards the goal, instead of sweeping the entire slide bar in both directions before solving. The response also tells you whether it is recommended to skip the current challenge, which happens when the ball and the goal cannot be reliably located in the image. The Python client (`pip install paripulse-captcha-solver`) will automatically call this endpoint and use the result. For non-python applications it is recommended to re-implement the code contained in the `paripulse-captcha-solver` GitHub repository in your preferred language.
### Making the API call
```py
import requests
import base64

BASE_URL = 'https://www.sadcaptcha.com/api/v1'
LICENSE_KEY = 'YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'


# Build the pre-analyze URL
pre_analyze_url = f'{BASE_URL}/paripulse-soccer-pre-analyze?licenseKey={LICENSE_KEY}'

# Convert the image to base64 encoding
with open('images/captcha.png', 'rb') as f:
    captcha = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

# Prepare the request
data = {
    'imageB64': captcha
}

# Get the drag direction and the ball and goal locations
r = requests.post(pre_analyze_url, json=data)

print(r.json())
```
### Using the solution
The response contains four fields:
- `leftOrRight` - the direction the ball needs to be dragged in, either `left` or `right`.
- `ballLocation` - the location of the ball as `proportionX` and `proportionY` of the image width and height.
- `targetLocation` - the location of the goal as `proportionX` and `proportionY` of the image width and height.
- `skipRecommended` - `true` if it is recommended to refresh the captcha instead of attempting to solve it.

Multiply the proportions by the width and height of the captcha image to obtain the pixel locations of the ball and the goal. Drag the slide button in the direction given by `leftOrRight`, recording a screenshot at each pixel, then send those screenshots to the `/paripulse-soccer` endpoint.
